newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-OSCAR DE LA HOYA DEFENCE POSTPONED.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-OSCAR DE LA HOYA DEFENCE POSTPONED.

text.p: Oscar de la Hoya, the World Boxing Council junior welterweight champion, has postponed his Oct. 12 title fight against Miguel Angel Gonzalez due to tendinitis in his left shoulder.

Both the WBC and de la Hoya's promoter, Top Rank Boxing, said Wednesday that the Las Vegas fight has been postponed, not cancelled. The injury is not serious enough for surgery, but de la Hoya needs rest for the injury to heal properly.
This is the second time the fight has been pushed back. It was originally scheduled for Sept. 14, but was postponed when heavyweight champion Mike Tyson had to reschedule his bout with Bruce Seldon.
The undercard of the fight, super lightweight Julio Cesar Chavez against Joey Gamache, was also postponed.
Top Rank Boxing spokesman Lee Samuels said they have a tentative date of Jan. 18 -- a Monday -- for the makeup date.
De la Hoya is 22-0 with 20 knockouts. He knocked out Chavez in the fourth round in June to win the WBC super lightweight title.
Gonzalez is 41-0 with 31 knockouts. He is a former lightweight champion but gave up his belt to fight big-name opponents in heavier weight classes.
